stories.name: Boeing stock outlook
stories.blurb: Investors are weighing whether to buy, hold, or sell Boeing shares amid earnings and shifting market sentiment.

stories.name: Archer-Boeing Deal
stories.blurb: Archer Aviation is acquiring Boeing subsidiaries Wisk Aero, Insitu, and SkyGrid, a deal that boosts Archer's growth prospects and stock price in the eVTOL/air taxi market.

stories.name: GE Aerospace Earnings
stories.blurb: GE Aerospace is posting strong, record earnings and raising its profit outlook on robust engine demand, but investors are questioning whether the stock's rally has already priced in its growth.

stories.name: Boeing 737 Max certification
stories.blurb: The FAA's long-delayed certification of Boeing's 737 Max 7 and Max 10 variants, complicated by software issues and safety concerns.

stories.name: Aerospace Q3 earnings
stories.blurb: Third-quarter earnings results and investor reaction across major aerospace companies, including Boeing, GE Aerospace, Hexcel, Honeywell, RTX, and United Airlines.

stories.name: Boeing F/A-XX Contract Win
stories.blurb: Boeing won a roughly $20 billion U.S. Navy contract to build the next-generation F/A-XX carrier fighter jet, sending its stock higher and opening a long-term defense revenue stream.

stories.name: Defense Stocks Surge
stories.blurb: Rising government defense spending, missile stockpile initiatives, and strong earnings are driving a broad rally in defense and aerospace stocks like Lockheed Martin, RTX, and Rocket Lab.

past.name: Boeing 737 Max certification
past.blurb: Boeing is working through regulatory certification and production delays for its 737 Max variants while trying to stabilize output.

past.name: Boeing Regulatory & Orders Update
past.blurb: Boeing navigates FAA regulatory approvals, safety inspections, and emissions exemptions while securing new aircraft orders and deliveries across its commercial jet lineup.

GE Aerospace posts record Q3 results
Boeing Q3 EPS misses, revenue beats

5.text: Boeing reported mixed Q3 2026 results with revenue in line but an EPS miss, a quarterly loss, and $464 million in free cash flow. Shares fell about 10.7% to $168.18 on delivery delays, a reduced 2026 delivery outlook, and cash flow doubts, though the MAX 10 was certified and the backlog hit a record.

6.text: ARK Investment Management bought over 1 million Archer shares, and Archer unveiled plans for three Texas air taxi networks. Analyst coverage remains cautious, citing FAA certification delays and patent litigation.

11.text: GE Aerospace’s quarter and stock valuation drew analyst scrutiny, while AerCap beat earnings estimates with adjusted EPS of $6.56, raised guidance, and saw shares rise about 4%. These articles barely mention Boeing, bearing on it only indirectly through aerospace suppliers and lessors.

8.text: The FAA approved the 737 MAX 10 after a nine-year wait, while Boeing's first 737-10 rolled out of a new Everett line. Boeing delayed its 737 Max production ramp to late 2027, expects 777-9 certification by mid-2027, and reported supplier shortages halting 777 freighter production and pushing 777-8 deliveries past 2030.

12.text: Hexcel beat Q3 EPS estimates but missed revenue, with commercial aerospace sales up 20.5% and stock falling 11.8%; it reaffirmed 2026 guidance on higher aircraft production. Honeywell also reported Q3 earnings. Both suppliers' results bear on Boeing indirectly through aerospace demand.

10.text: Boeing is named only as a listed player in three market reports (counter-drone, military drones, unmanned sea systems), while its Spirit Defense unit will partner with GA-ASI to produce the FQ-42 collaborative combat aircraft. Other articles cover Lockheed, BAE and battery-manufacturing news without Boeing involvement.

7.text: Boeing missed earnings and its stock tumbled, at one point down 11%, dragging the Dow lower. Broader markets rose as AI and chip stocks rallied on Anthropic news ahead of the Fed meeting.

9.text: The FAA certified the 737 MAX 10 on October 20, unlocking over 1,555 orders that make up more than 30% of Boeing's 737 backlog. A dispute with supplier Vaero halted 777 freighter production.
